hotspots.title: Lecture hall
hotspots.text: The lecturer presents a simple case and asks the class who should win and why. The point is to practise reasoning from rules, not memorizing answers.
hotspots.fact: Legal thinking means applying rules to facts.

hotspots.title: Law library
hotspots.text: You search through statutes and past court decisions to find the rule that fits a case, and mark the parts that matter.
hotspots.fact: Careful reading is the core skill of the whole major.

hotspots.title: Moot court
hotspots.text: You stand up and argue a small case in front of a mock judge, who interrupts you with questions you did not expect.
hotspots.fact: Moot court lets students practise arguing live.

hotspots.title: Legal clinic
hotspots.text: You listen to a client explain a problem, then help draft a document that states their situation clearly and correctly.
hotspots.fact: Listening and clear writing matter as much as knowing the law.

hotspots.title: Law firm
hotspots.text: As an intern you prepare case files, check details, and watch how lawyers handle real deadlines.
hotspots.fact: Law graduates work in firms, companies, government, and many other places.
